payload.task_text:
You are a developer community organizer preparing to attend China Tech Expo 2026, a technology conference held at the Qufu International Convention Center from March 13 to March 14, 2026. Your task is to research relevant technology topics by finding the most popular videos from a well-known short-form tech channel, plan your train travel from Beijing to Qufu and back, organize all information into a structured spreadsheet, document the complete plan in your team knowledge base, and add all key events to the shared calendar.

Begin by searching for the top 5 most-viewed videos from the Fireship channel on the video platform, sorted by popularity. For each video, retrieve the full title, view count, approximate duration in minutes, and a brief description of the key technologies discussed. Identify the primary technology topic covered in each video so you can prepare relevant knowledge before the conference sessions.

Next, look up the train station codes for Beijing South station and Qufu East station using the train booking system. Query available high-speed trains departing Beijing South and arriving at Qufu East on March 12, 2026. Select the most suitable after-work evening departure train for the outbound journey. Then query return trains from Qufu East to Beijing South on March 15, 2026, and select a suitable afternoon return train. Retrieve the intermediate stop information for both selected trains.

Check the shared calendar to see any existing events between March 12 and March 15, 2026, and note any potential conflicts.

Create an Excel workbook named Tech_Conference_Plan.xlsx in your workspace. It must contain three sheets. The first sheet should be named Prep_Videos and contain columns: Rank, Title, Topic, View_Count, Duration_Min, and Key_Technologies. Populate it with the 5 videos you retrieved, ranked from most to least viewed. The second sheet should be named Travel_Details and contain columns: Leg, Train_No, From_Station, To_Station, Departure, Arrival, Duration_Min, Seat_Class, and Price_CNY. Add one row for the outbound journey and one row for the return journey, using the train codes and actual departure/arrival times you retrieved. Use first class for both legs and look up the actual price from the rail system for each leg. Record the station names and the seat class exactly as returned by the rail booking system (the system reports them in Chinese, e.g. 北京南 / 曲阜东 / 一等座) — do not translate them. The third sheet should be named Conference_Schedule and contain columns: Date, Time, Activity, Location, and Notes. Add at least six rows covering departure on March 12, conference day one sessions and activities on March 13, conference day two sessions and networking on March 14, and the return journey on March 15; the exact activities and times in this schedule are up to you. Write all cell values in the workbook as literal values (plain numbers and text) — do not use Excel formulas.

Create a page in the team knowledge base titled "Tech Conference Preparation - Qufu March 2026". The page should include a travel details section describing both train journeys with the actual train numbers, departure and arrival times, and station names you retrieved. It should also include a Learning Resources section listing the five video topics you identified, with a brief note on why each technology topic is relevant to conference preparation.

Finally, add the following events to the shared calendar: a travel event titled "Conference Travel: Beijing to Qufu" on March 12 from 17:00 to 20:00; a full-day conference event titled "Tech Conference Day 1" on March 13 from 09:00 to 18:00; a second full-day conference event titled "Tech Conference Day 2" on March 14 from 09:00 to 18:00; and a return travel event titled "Return: Qufu to Beijing" on March 15 from 14:30 to 17:30.

Configuration details for this task are provided in the file conference_config.json and general preparation guidelines are in prep_guide.md, both located in your workspace.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use two dependency waves with exactly four sub-agents. Video research and train planning are independent; after they return, the workbook and knowledge-base page can be written in parallel from one frozen plan.

Before Wave 1, dynamically resolve and read `conference_config.json` plus `prep_guide.md`. Freeze the channel, top-five ranking rule, station/date/seat preferences, conference schedule requirements, exact four calendar slots, and any conflict-handling guidance. Use `list_events` once for an ISO range covering 2026-03-12 through 2026-03-16 with a sufficiently large `maxResults`, then inspect title/time overlaps locally. In the same response that dispatches Wave 1, create only missing fixed events with `create_event` using exact ISO `start.dateTime`/`end.dateTime` values; retain every returned event ID.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 Explore sub-agents in parallel:

   1. explore 0 (web-domain-researcher 0): Use one Explore sub-agent to own one complete read-only Fireship channel catalog session. Obtain the channel/video-list identifier, continue the returned list identifier with the platform's navigation cursor/page operation until source exhaustion, and retrieve details only as needed for complete title, integer view count, duration, description, and tags. Rank the whole observed catalog by view count descending with a stable Video_ID tie-break and return exactly the verified top five with rank, duration minutes, one evidence-supported primary topic, key technologies, and catalog page/row/duplicate controls. Do not stop after the first page or write artifacts.

   2. explore 1 (web-domain-researcher 1): Use one Explore sub-agent to own the complete read-only travel branch. Resolve Beijing South and Qufu East station codes through the station lookup; query 2026-03-12 outbound and 2026-03-15 return tickets with the resolved codes; select a task-suitable after-work evening outbound and afternoon return by actual times, availability, and first-class (`一等座`) evidence; then retrieve intermediate stops for exactly those two selected train/date pairs. Return one compact two-leg table preserving actual Chinese station/seat labels, train numbers, timestamps, duration, first-class price, and stop-list/ticket coverage. Do not invent a price or translate returned labels.

After Wave 1, the main agent validates top-five order, two journey constraints, seat/price evidence, stop coverage, and calendar conflicts, then freezes one immutable conference-plan payload including at least six schedule rows.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 Coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one Coder sub-agent as the sole writer of `Tech_Conference_Plan.xlsx`. Create the exact three sheets from the frozen payload with exact headers/order, five videos, two travel legs, at least six schedule rows, and literal values only. Read all sheets back and return path plus row/value checks.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Use one Coder sub-agent as the sole owner of the exact-title `Tech Conference Preparation - Qufu March 2026` page. Search exact title, create or complete one nonduplicate page with both actual train journeys and all five learning topics/relevance notes, retrieve it, and return ID plus coverage checks.

After Wave 2, the main agent reconciles train/video facts across both artifacts, retrieves each created/reused calendar event with `get_event(eventId)`, preserves unrelated conflicts, and verifies all original outputs without a third wave.

nodes.text:
You are gathering read-only research for a developer-community organizer who is preparing for "China Tech Expo 2026". Your job: find the TOP 5 MOST-VIEWED videos from the **Fireship** YouTube channel, sorted by popularity, and extract precise details for each.

Context you need:
- The Fireship channel is a well-known short-form tech education channel. Its YouTube channel ID is `UCsBjURrPoezykLs9EqgamOA` (verify this with `mcp__youtube__channels_getChannel` if useful; if that ID is wrong, find the correct one by searching).
- You have YouTube tools: `mcp__youtube__channels_getChannel`, `mcp__youtube__channels_listVideos` (accepts `sortOrder` of `newest`, `oldest`, or `popular`), `mcp__youtube__channels_navigateList`, `mcp__youtube__videos_getVideo`, `mcp__youtube__videos_searchVideos`.
- This is a READ-ONLY task. Do not attempt to write, modify, or create anything anywhere.

Steps:
1. Call `mcp__youtube__channels_listVideos` with channelId `UCsBjURrPoezykLs9EqgamOA`, `sortOrder` = `popular`, and `maxResults` = 20. This gives videos sorted by popularity (most viewed first).
2. Take the TOP 5 videos from that popularity-sorted list.
3. For each of those 5 videos, retrieve full details using `mcp__youtube__videos_getVideo` with `parts` = ["snippet", "contentDetails", "statistics"] so you get: exact `title`, exact `viewCount` (statistics), `duration` (ISO-8601, from contentDetails), and `description` (snippet).
4. Convert each ISO-8601 duration to approximate minutes (round to the nearest minute; e.g. PT10M28S ≈ 10 minutes).

Deliverables — report back a compact, structured summary containing, for EACH of the top 5 videos (ranked 1 = most viewed through 5 = least viewed):
- `rank` (1-5)
- `video_id`
- `title` (the full, exact title text)
- `view_count` (exact integer as reported by the API)
- `duration_min` (approximate whole minutes)
- `key_technologies` (2-4 short phrases naming the specific languages / frameworks / tools / concepts the video actually covers, derived from the title and description)
- `primary_topic` (one concise label for the single main technology topic, e.g. "Web Frameworks", "Programming Language", "AI / LLMs", "Cloud & DevOps")
- `description` (one or two sentences summarizing what the video discusses)

Also report: the channel's exact name and channel ID as confirmed, and the video IDs / view counts of videos ranked 6-8 (so I can sanity-check the ranking cut-off).

Be precise with numbers — do not round view counts or invent values. If the popularity-sorted list and per-video statistics disagree, trust the per-video `statistics.viewCount` from `videos_getVideo`, but keep the ranking order from the popularity-sorted list. Report exactly what the tools return.
Research top Fireship videos

You are gathering read-only research for a developer-community organizer traveling from Beijing to Qufu for "China Tech Expo 2026" (held at Qufu International Convention Center on 2026-03-13 and 2026-03-14). Your job: look up China railway (12306) station codes, high-speed train options for two legs, and the intermediate stops of the two trains I will select.

You have read-only 12306 tools: `mcp__rail_12306__get-station-code-by-names`, `mcp__rail_12306__get-station-code-of-citys`, `mcp__rail_12306__get-stations-code-in-city`, `mcp__rail_12306__get-station-by-telecode`, `mcp__rail_12306__get-tickets`, `mcp__rail_12306__get-interline-tickets`, `mcp__rail_12306__get-train-route-stations`. This is a READ-ONLY research task — do not book or modify anything.

Important rules:
- NEVER pass Chinese station names directly to `get-tickets`; you must first resolve them to `station_code` via `get-station-code-by-names`.
- Keep all Chinese text exactly as the system returns it (e.g. 北京南, 曲阜东, 一等座). Do not translate.

Steps:
1. Call `mcp__rail_12306__get-station-code-by-names` with stationNames `北京南|曲阜东` to get both station codes. Report the code for each.
2. OUTBOUND: call `mcp__rail_12306__get-tickets` with date `2026-03-12`, fromStation = the 北京南 code, toStation = the 曲阜东 code, `trainFilterFlags` = `G`, `earliestStartTime` = 16, `latestStartTime` = 23, `sortFlag` = `startTime`. This is an after-work evening departure on a Thursday.
3. RETURN: call `mcp__rail_12306__get-tickets` with date `2026-03-15`, fromStation = the 曲阜东 code, toStation = the 北京南 code, `trainFilterFlags` = `G`, `earliestStartTime` = 12, `latestStartTime` = 19, `sortFlag` = `startTime`. This should be an afternoon departure.
4. From each result set, identify the most suitable train:
   - Outbound: an evening departure after normal working hours (roughly 17:00-19:30 departure from 北京南) that arrives at 曲阜东 the same evening. Prefer a direct G train with the most sensible arrival time and available 一等座 (first class) tickets. Avoid anything departing before 17:00.
   - Return: an early-to-mid afternoon departure from 曲阜东 (roughly 13:30-16:00) arriving 北京南 in the late afternoon / early evening, with available 一等座.
   - State clearly which train you picked for each leg and why.
5. For EACH of the two selected trains, call `mcp__rail_12306__get-train-route-stations` with the train's internal `train_no` (the long code like `240000G10336`, NOT the short code like `G1033`), the `fromStationTelecode` and `toStationTelecode` of that leg's journey, and the corresponding `departDate` (`2026-03-12` for outbound, `2026-03-15` for return). Report the full list of intermediate stops with station name, arrival time, departure time, and stopover duration.

Deliverables — report back in a compact, structured form:
A. Station codes for 北京南 and 曲阜东 (code + name exactly as returned).
B. OUTBOUND candidates: for every train in the 2026-03-12 evening window, a row with: 车次 (train code like `G105`), departure time, arrival time, total duration, 一等座 availability and its exact price in CNY, plus any other seat classes shown. Include the internal `train_no` and the from/to telecodes.
C. RETURN candidates: the same for the 2026-03-15 afternoon window.
D. Your selected outbound train and selected return train, with full details (train code, internal train_no, telecodes, departure time, arrival time, duration, 一等座 price).
E. The intermediate-stop list (经停站) for each of the two selected trains, in order, with station names, arrival/departure times and stop durations.

Be exact with times and prices — copy them verbatim from the tool output. If a query returns no results, say so explicitly and widen the time window slightly and report what you found.
Research Beijing-Qufu rail options
